provider: CSC Fairdata IDA (Finland) — quota granted per CSC project, funded from the home organisation's national TB pool

free_tier.stated: No flat per-user number; the quota is a slice of your organisation's allocation. Published national pool (last updated 2025-02-28): University of Helsinki 1,500 TB, Aalto 480 TB, University of Oulu 465 TB, University of Turku 427 TB, Tampere universities 361.7 TB, Åbo Akademi 150 TB, and so on. You apply for a number of GiB in MyCSC and your organisation's IDA contact person approves it, 'usually within a few working days'.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Free; IDA is a CSC national service and 'The use of Fairdata IDA doesn't consume Billing Units.'

tooling: IDA web UI plus official command-line tools ('or use IDA's command line tools'); publication path is Qvain + download through the Fairdata download service.
chaining: Quota is per project and drawn from an institutional pool, and a CSC project 'does not have to correspond to a specific research project, and it can have only one member'. So many small projects each drawing a quota slice, each approved by the same institutional contact. The 1.5 PB Helsinki pool is the real ceiling.

limits.value: Approval. Two gates, one of them human.

limits_note: Per-object-cap: not published. Retention: 'Data can be stored for a duration at least as long as the allocation grant period' (DeiC analogue); IDA requires an active CSC project and 'The validity of your CSC account can be extended by logging in to CSC's services'. request-rate: not published. Gate: CSC account (Haka/Virtu) + institutional quota owner approval. Two gates, one of them human.

identity_cost.detail: storage is granted to a CSC project, and the grant is approved by the IDA contact person of the home organisation named as the project's Storage Quota Owner, usually within a few working days. A CSC user account is created through the Finnish Haka or Virtu identity federations, or by applying to the CSC service desk as a collaborator of a Finnish research group or as a user whose organisation holds a contract with CSC. A CSC project can have a single member. No card and no phone number is asked for; the multi-factor setup asks for an authenticator app on a mobile device.

reliability_note: Second gate is a human approver at your home organisation; a lapsed CSC account or project takes the storage with it.

extras.agent_focus: National and regional research-data infrastructure that hands out free (or grant-funded) bulk object storage to researchers: EUDAT/B2SHARE, EOSC EU Node, SURF, GÉANT ecosystem, NIRD/Sigma2, CSC Allas + LUMI-O, NAISS, DeiC, EuroHPC, DARIAH/CLARIN/ELIXIR nodes, NCI, ARDC Nectar, Digital Alliance of Canada, ACCESS/OSN, TACC, NCAR, NRP. Central question: which of these are SELF-SERVICE (anyone can get a login and a bucket) versus INSTITUTION-GATED (you need a university appointment, a national research affiliation, or a reviewed proposal). The per-project quotas here are the largest numbers in the whole survey — 10-150 TB — so the gate, not the quota, is the finding.
